subject: Commercial clarifications: metering lag, carryforward credits, and pro-rata smoothing
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@omnihealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@omnihealth.com
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Commercial section — a few metering and billing questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the initial RFP response last week. Procurement and finance have a couple of focused clarifications on the commercial appendix before we move to legal:

1) Metering lag: Our billing system expects usage files every Monday for prior-week usage. How do you handle ingestion delays and what lookback window do you use for true-ups? Is there a standard 14-day metering lag you operate with?

2) Carryforward credits: If our monthly usage falls below the committed floor one month but exceeds it the next, can unused committed units carry forward within a quarter? If not, can you describe any grace windows or pro-rata smoothing you offer to avoid sharp monthly overages?

3) Pro-rata billing window: For ramp months where we expect a mid-month go-live, will you pro-rate the commit for the partial month or require full-month commit?

4) Overage rates and caps: Please confirm overage price per 1M tokens and whether you support an overage cap (percent of committed spend) to limit surprise charges.

I attached an XLS with line items where our procurement team would prefer numeric fields filled in. Can someone from pricing respond with specific line-item values (e.g., token price, embedding price, overage ladder) and examples for a 6-month ramp scenario?

Thanks —
Sophie
Sophie Martin
Head of Procurement | OmniHealth
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@omnihealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-09T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Commercial section — a few metering and billing questions

Sophie —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Laura (billing ops) to provide the numeric examples and operational notes. High level answers below; Ben will follow with a short spreadsheet and concrete numbers by EOD tomorrow.

- Metering lag: Our hosted billing uses an event-driven metering feed but we support weekly aggregated usage files. We typically allow a 14-day reconciliation window after month-end for late events (default), with a longer 30-day reconciliation on negotiated contracts. True-ups for missed events are applied in the subsequent invoice period.

- Carryforward credits: We offer a single-quarter carryforward for unused committed token volumes by default for annual commitments (i.e., unused units in Q1 can be used in Q2). For shorter terms or month-to-month, carryforward is not enabled but we can provide a one-time grace band during initial ramp months.

- Pro-rata billing window: We pro-rate the committed units for the first partial month based on days in service (simple pro-rata). If you need pro-rating at a weekly granularity for pilot phases, that's configurable but requires invoicing note.

- Overage rates and caps: Standard overage is priced at a % premium over the committed unit price (typical starting point is 25% premium per 1M-token equivalent), but we support a soft cap where overage spend is capped at X% of committed monthly spend (negotiable). We will detail two options when we share the spreadsheet: conservative (lower overage premium + 5% cap) and protective (higher premium + no cap).

Ben — please attach the pricing appendix with the illustrative 6-month ramp math and the token/embedding per-unit prices. Laura — can you add operational notes about billing cutoff times, invoice timing and when credits would be applied?

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@omnihealth.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-10T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Commercial section — a few metering and billing questions (pricing appendix attached)

Hi Sophie — attaching the pricing appendix (Redwood_Pricing_Appendix_v1.pdf) and an Excel with worked examples (OmniHealth_RFP_Commercial_Questions.xlsx). Key items called out below — I've put example numbers for a 6-month ramp from 0 -> 60M tokens/month.

1) Unit pricing (illustrative):
- Committed token price (per 1M tokens): $80 (flat for generation tokens)
- Embedding token price (per 1M tokens): $150
- Overage price (per 1M tokens): $100 (25% premium over committed)

2) Tiering and smoothing:
- If monthly usage exceeds committed units, first 20% overage billed at 10% premium instead of full overage rate (this is the soft-band smoothing we apply for early burst), remaining overage billed at full overage price. This is intended to reduce jumpiness during ramp months.

3) Carryforward and true-up:
- For annual committed contracts we allow carryforward within the same quarter up to 50% of the unused monthly committed volume (e.g., month A unused units can offset month B up to 50% of B's commit).
- Reconciliation window: default 14 days after month-end; delayed events after reconciliation are processed in next invoice with a line-item true-up. If you opt for 30-day reconciliation, the billing cycle shifts to accommodate the longer lookback.

4) Metering lag handling:
- We stamp events with generated-at and ingested-at times. For reconciliation we rely on ingested-at; late ingestion beyond the reconciliation window is flagged and credited in the following invoice.

5) Pro-rata example (mid-month go-live):
- If go-live on day 16 of a 30-day month for a 10M/month commit, pro-rated commit = 10M * (15/30) = 5M for first invoice period. Overages within that partial month billed against the pro-rated commit.

6) Overage cap options:
- Option A (protective): 5% cap on monthly overage spend — Redwood absorbs overage beyond that cap for the month and credits on next invoice.
- Option B (neutral): no cap, but tiered overage ladder as described in #2.

I've put the line-item per-unit values and three ramp scenarios in the attached XLS. If you prefer, we can convert this to a monthly amortized invoice schedule for your finance team.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference

Attachments: OmniHealth_RFP_Commercial_Questions.xlsx, Redwood_Pricing_Appendix_v1.pdf

- Confirm ability to switch reconciliation window to 30 days for our first two quarters (we'll need the invoice timing aligned to that) — are there pricing or SLA implications?
- We like Option A (5% cap) for the pilot months only; please confirm whether that requires an additional contract addendum or can be included in the SOW.

If you can reply with the specific contract language for the 5% cap and a consolidated invoice schedule for a 6-month ramp (row-level numbers), we'll circulate to Legal this afternoon.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Ethan
